description: This file provides an example implementation of using Frame Buffer Object (FBO) in Kivy to optimize graphics rendering by drawing widgets onto an off-screen buffer and then displaying that buffer, including a custom layout class and a test application that creates many buttons.

classes.name: FboFloatLayout
classes.description: A custom layout that uses an Fbo to optimize widget rendering by redirecting graphics instructions to an off-screen buffer.

classes.name: TestFboApp
classes.description: A test application demonstrating the use of FboFloatLayout with a large number of buttons.

methods.name: __init__
methods.description: Initializes the FboFloatLayout, creating a canvas, Fbo, and rectangle, and setting up the texture property.

methods.name: add_widget
methods.description: Overrides add_widget to attach graphics instructions to the Fbo instead of the main canvas.

methods.name: remove_widget
methods.description: Overrides remove_widget to detach graphics instructions from the Fbo.

methods.name: on_size
methods.description: Updates the size of the Fbo and rectangle when the layout size changes.

methods.name: on_pos
methods.description: Updates the position of the rectangle when the layout position changes.

methods.name: on_texture
methods.description: Updates the rectangle's texture when the Fbo's texture changes.

methods.name: build
methods.description: Builds the test layout with 5000 buttons, demonstrating the Fbo's performance benefits.
